item.description: The Fisheries and Aquaculture Division (NFI) is responsible for the economic, social, institutional, governance and policy aspects of FAO’s activities related to fisheries and aquaculture and their development, with particular emphasis on human well-being, food security and poverty reduction; post-harvest utilization, marketing and trade with due regard to the protection of the environment, food security and the well-being of fishing communities; collection, compilation, validation, trend analysis and dissemination of the best available and up-to-date fishery statistics and for the syndication of the FAO information on all aspects of world fisheries and aquaculture.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Fisheries and Aquaculture Division (NFI) is responsible for the economic, social, institutional, governance and policy aspects of FAO’s activities related to fisheries and aquaculture and their development, with particular emphasis on human well-being, food security and poverty reduction; post-harvest utilization, marketing and trade with due regard to the protection of the environment, food security and the well-being of fishing communities; collection, compilation, validation, trend analysis and dissemination of the best available and up-to-date fishery statistics and for the syndication of the FAO information on all aspects of world fisheries and aquaculture. The Division is also responsible for FAO’s activities related to the management and conservation of the living aquatic resources used by fisheries and aquaculture, including the biodiversity and ecosystem maintenance, with particular emphasis on most vulnerable and threatened species and habitats; management of responsible fisheries and aquaculture in accordance with modern management standards and best practices; development of fisheries technology, with due regard to the protection of the environment, food security and the well-being of fishing communities, including the safety of fishers and fishing vessels.

The position is located in the Fisheries and Aquaculture Division, NFI, in the Global Processes and Institutions Team (NFIPI), at FAO headquarters in Rome, Italy

Reporting Lines

The Fishery Officer (Climate Change) reports to the Fishery Resources Officer, NFIPI, in charge of coordinating the climate change work across the Fisheries and Aquaculture Division.

Technical Focus

The Fishery Officer (Climate Change) contributes to activities aimed at strengthening the climate resilience of the fisheries and aquaculture sector, including the integration of climate considerations into fisheries and aquaculture management, policy development, programmes and projects at global, regional and national levels. The incumbent supports the provision of technical assistance, policy analysis, knowledge products, project implementation, and capacity-development activities, drawing on an understanding of the impacts of climate change on marine and inland fisheries, aquaculture and aquatic food systems, and their associated social, economic and environmental dimensions. The position also supports complementary activities across the team’s broader portfolio of global fisheries governance processes and institutions, as determined by emerging priorities and work programme needs.

Key Results

Collection and analysis of information, data and statistics and project/meeting services to support programme projects, products and services.

Key Functions

• Collects and analyses relevant technical, social, economic, environmental, institutional and technology related information, data and/or statistics to support the delivery of programme projects, as well as products and services.

• Undertakes analysis, provides technical input for plans and reports and edits/revises technical/scientific documents.

• Participates in the development of improved work methods, tools and systems.

• Updates databases and web pages.

• Participates in multidisciplinary project/work teams.

• Collaborates in the development of training tools and materials and the organization of workshops/seminars, etc.

• Participates in the organization, conduct and follow-up of meetings, consultations and conferences, the development/production of required materials and the provision of information and assistance to partners.

Specific Functions

• Supports the NFI contribution to the implementation of the FAO Strategy on climate change.

• Assists in the follow-up to relevant Committee on Fisheries (COFI) requests on climate change, specifically on development of tools, guidance on adaptation and mitigation.

• Assists in the preparation of FAO’s contribution to global events related to climate change, in particular under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change processes and events (Conference of Parties, Subsidiary Body for Scientific and Technological Advice, Ocean Dialogue, etc.).

• Provides assistance to resource mobilization work by putting together material of relevance to donors, for example by contributing to the content development and publication of climate change knowledge products.

• Provides assistance to the implementation of fisheries and aquaculture field projects on climate change as required (e.g. organization of workshops, reporting) and the development of field project concept notes as appropriate.

• Supports the coordination work for the NFI Working Group on climate change (e.g. internal meetings, information sharing channels) and for a wider network on climate change in fisheries and aquaculture if needed.

• Assists in the liaison with other FAO Divisions/Offices/Centres and Decentralized Offices and contributes to corporate inputs in international climate-related processes and events, as well as resource mobilization.

• Contributes to the update and management of the NFI climate change projects inventory, as well as the compilation of climate change publications.

• Assists in the organization of and participates in relevant meetings, conferences, seminars and workshops as required.

• Performs other related duties as required.

CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING

Minimum Requirements

• Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in biology, fishery science, marine ecology, economics, fisheries economics, fisheries management, ocean governance or other related field.

• Three years of relevant experience in fishery (and/or aquaculture) research, science, management, trade, statistics and data, ocean governance or related field.

• Working knowledge (proficiency - level C) of English and intermediate knowledge (intermediate proficiency - level B) of another FAO official language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish).

Competencies

• Results Focus

• Teamwork

• Communication

• Building effective relationships

• Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement

Technical/Functional Skills

• Work experience in more than one location or area of work, particularly in field positions, is desirable.

• Extent and relevance of experience working in an international context, including with international organizations, governments, regional bodies or other international institutions.

• Extent and relevance of experience in collecting and analysing technical information and data.

• Extent and relevance of knowledge and experience in related fields such as fisheries, fish taxonomy and ecology.

• Extent and relevance of experience in the preparation, editing and revision of technical/scientific documents and in organizing meetings and workshops.

• Extent and relevance of experience in working with scientific bibliographic databases and/or information systems, in editing/publishing scientific documents.

The Regional Producer Engagement Specialists work with CDFA Farm to School Regional Network Leads, the CDFA Farm to School Network, and regional partners to create solutions that serve the California school food community and advance CDFA’s Farm to School Roadmap.

This position will serve the Bay Area Region, which includes the following counties: Sonoma, Marin, Napa, Solano, Contra Costa, Alameda, Santa Clara, San Mateo, and San Francisco.

item.title: Assistant Professor in Community Economic Development at University of Wisconsin-Madison
item.description: The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics (AAE) in the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS), together with the Division of Extension (EXT) at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in community economic development.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics (AAE) in the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS), together with the Division of Extension (EXT) at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in community economic development. This is a jointly appointed faculty position to both AAE and the Department of Extension, with the tenure home in AAE. Within Extension, the candidate will affiliate with the Community Development Institute. The position is funded 75% EXT/ 25% CALS and structured as a 12-month appointment. Given the outreach expectations of the Extension appointment, there is no requirement for traditional group instruction in the undergraduate or graduate program.

The ideal candidate has demonstrated research potential in rural and/or community economic development and complements existing departmental strengths in agricultural, environmental, community, and/or development economics. We seek candidates with evidence of the ability to combine rigorous economic research with effective outreach and who have demonstrated a strong commitment to public engagement and real-world impact.

As a faculty member, the candidate will lead regionally and nationally recognized research, outreach, and educational programming focused on community economic development within the United States, with relevance to Wisconsin. They will design and conduct applied research to address challenges facing rural communities. The faculty member will translate research findings into practical, accessible resources for stakeholders, such as local governments, nonprofit organizations, and community leaders. The faculty member is expected to support the university’s mission of fostering inclusive, sustainable community growth, as well as the scholarly life of the department through collegial engagement, mentorship, and service.

This position offers an outstanding opportunity for impact by working at a top land-grant institution, joining an established network of community development professionals across the state and nationally, and working directly with local leaders and communities.

Additional Information:

At the University of Wisconsin-Madison, the Division of Extension collaborates with many departments to hire, fund, and tenure faculty who generate research directly applicable to Wisconsin communities and outreach in support of Extension programming. These co-funded faculty work collaboratively with Extension educators, other faculty, and external partners through research, outreach, and extramural funding opportunities related to their subject-matter expertise. While tenured in the department of their field of study, Extension activities are a significant portion of their duties and performance evaluation.

The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics at UW–Madison is internationally recognized for its research and teaching in agricultural, environmental, community, and development economics. Faculty collaborate across disciplines to address complex global and local challenges. UW–Madison is located in Madison, Wisconsin—an innovative and vibrant city frequently ranked among the best places to live in the U.S. The university fosters a collaborative and inclusive environment and is committed to diversity, equity, and community engagement.

Key Job Responsibilities:

  • Publish scholarly and applied research on community economic development in U.S. and relevant to communities in Wisconsin on topics such as workforce development, housing, entrepreneurship, local government capacity, and regional economic resilience.

  • Develop an extension program that translates and applies research-based knowledge and methods to issues and problems facing Wisconsin communities and document the impact of these efforts.

  • Work with interdisciplinary teams within CALS, Extension, and across UW–Madison, to advance integrated approaches to solving real-world challenges in Wisconsin and rural America.

  • Engage with stakeholders, including industry leaders, policymakers, and community groups on community development issues.

  • Secure extramural funding to support research and programming.

  • Mentor students at all levels and contribute to curriculum development.

  • Participate in departmental, college, and university committees, as well as relevant professional associations and public service activities.

  • Contribute to a supportive and inclusive academic environment.

Department: Agricultural and Applied Economics

Compensation: Negotiable, 12-month

Required Qualifications:

  • Training or experience demonstrating potential for excellence in conducting frontier research and actively engaging in outreach.

  • Demonstrated skill in statistical data analysis, managing large datasets, and complex problem-solving.

  • Demonstrated subject-matter expertise in relevant topic areas such as community economic development, rural development, and regional science.

  • A record of, or demonstrated potential for, securing competitive external funding.

  • Demonstrated ability or potential for strong public engagement, interdisciplinary collaboration, and stakeholder engagement.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills are required and will be assessed via written work listed on curriculum vitae, statements submitted for the application, and interactions during the interview process.

Education:

Required: Ph.D. in Agricultural Economics, Economics, or a related field, such as Urban and Regional Planning or Public Policy, by the start date.

Apply online at “Jobs at UW” (http://jobs.wisc.edu) under job number JR10015766. Applications must be received through UW-Madison’s online application system.

To begin the process, please click “Apply Now”.

4) An example of research such as a job market paper.

5) Contact information for two to three references who will submit letters of recommendation and may be contacted for a reference phone call at a later date.

item.title: Assistant Professor of Utah Water Policy at Utah State University
item.description: Utah State University’s Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics seeks an Assistant Professor in Natural Resource Economics, prioritizing water economics and policy relevant to Utah and the Intermountain West.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
Utah State University’s Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics seeks an Assistant Professor in Natural Resource Economics, prioritizing water economics and policy relevant to Utah and the Intermountain West.

This is a nine-month, tenure-track, academic-year appointment with a role of 50% teaching, 45% research, 5% service located in Logan, UT.

Responsibilities

  • Teach undergraduate and graduate courses, face-to-face or online, in environmental and natural resource economics, benefit-cost or policy analysis, applied microeconomics, or quantitative methods, according to departmental needs.

  • Develop a nationally recognized research program in water economics and policy, including conservation, allocation, agricultural water use, or policy Related work on land use, public lands, ecosystem services, energy, or climate adaptation may complement this focus.

  • Publish high-quality peer-reviewed research and communicate findings to academic and policy audiences. Collaborate with state partners and Extension colleagues on policy briefs or decision

  • Seek external funding and pursue disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration within and beyond the

  • Mentor undergraduate and graduate students, serve on graduate supervisory committees, and contribute departmental, college, university, and professional service consistent with rank and appointment.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

  • A Ph.D. in economics, applied economics, agricultural economics, natural resource economics, or a closely related field by the start date;

  • Demonstrated potential for productive research and effective undergraduate and graduate teaching;

  • Strong quantitative, written, and oral communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

item.title: Manager/Associate Director/Director of Public Policy at National Association of State Departments of Agriculture
item.description: The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture is seeking a new team member to join its Public Policy team who is passionate about American agriculture and the policies that affect the agricultural industry.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture is seeking a new team member to join its Public Policy team who is passionate about American agriculture and the policies that affect the agricultural industry. This position serves as NASDA’s lead federal policy advocate for food systems and nutrition. The role converts member priorities into coordinated legislative, regulatory, and funding strategies; leads the Food Systems and Nutrition Committee; and builds the relationships needed to elevate the voice of state departments of agriculture food systems and nutrition policy. Depending on qualifications, experience, and capacity demonstrated, the portfolio may expand to include leadership of the Marketing and International Trade Committee and associated policy issues, providing a defined opportunity to take on broader responsibility over time.

This position will have the opportunity to travel across the U.S. for meetings and conferences with the possibility of international travel. The candidate will be able to build relationships and collaborate with leaders from state departments of agriculture from all 50 states and four U.S. territories, congressional and government entities, and agricultural partnerships and coalitions.

Members of the Public Policy team earn a competitive salary and enjoy an excellent work culture at an organization with exceptional perks, including a flexible schedule and an incredible mission.

ABOUT NASDA

The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture is a nonpartisan, nonprofit association representing the 50 elected and appointed commissioners, secretaries, and directors of the state departments of agriculture, and four U.S. territories. NASDA grows and enhances American agriculture through policy, partnerships, and public engagement. We recognize that to achieve our goals, we need employees as passionate about agriculture as we are. We strive to create a positive work environment that our employees can be proud of and where they can build their careers.

ABOUT THE POSITION

The essential functions include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Lead the development, implementation, and communication of NASDA’s federal policy portfolio for food systems and nutrition, with primary emphasis on funding and implementation of state led farm-to-table programs; additional priorities may include food safety (e.g., FSMA and food safety inspection), in close coordination with and support of NASDA’s Food Safety team, as well as food labeling, nutrition, food waste, food access and security, and food supply chain issues.

  • Serve as staff lead for the Food Systems and Nutrition Committee, coordinating priorities with the committee’s Chair and Vice-Chair, preparing meeting agendas, policy materials, recommendations, and follow-up actions.

  • Translate member priorities into legislative, regulatory, and appropriations strategies and advocate those positions before Congress and federal agencies.

  • Monitor and analyze federal legislation, regulations, funding opportunities, and emerging issues; provide timely, concise, decision-ready guidance to NASDA members and leadership.

  • Build trusted relationships with commissioners, secretaries, directors, and staff of state departments of agriculture and facilitate consensus across diverse state interests.

  • Develop and sustain partnerships and coalitions with agricultural, food systems and nutrition stakeholders to advance NASDA priorities and elevate the roles of state departments of agriculture in those spaces.

  • Draft high-quality policy briefs, testimony, comment letters, talking points, presentations, and member communications.

  • Manage projects, timelines, deliverables, and reporting with sound and strategic judgment.

  • Demonstrate readiness for increasing responsibility by building subject matter knowledge, independently managing assigned issues, and developing the judgment and stakeholder relationships needed to assume additional committee and policy leadership.

  • Collaborate across NASDA’s policy, communications, trade, partnerships, and other key teams and represent NASDA at meetings and events, including travel as required.

QUALIFICATIONS

Candidates may be considered at the Manager, Associate Director, or Director level based on the depth, scope, and relevance of their experience.

  1. Manager, Public Policy: At least two years of relevant experience, with demonstrated ability to support policy analysis and advocacy, manage defined issues and projects, cultivate stakeholder relationships, and produce clear, accurate written materials with appropriate guidance. The Manager is expected to grow toward greater independence and may assume additional policy or committee leadership based on demonstrated readiness, performance, and organizational needs.

  2. Associate Director, Public Policy: At least four years of relevant experience, with demonstrated ability to manage policy issues, relationships, and projects with increasing independence.

  3. Director, Public Policy: At least six years of relevant experience, including demonstrated ownership of complex policy strategy, senior level external representation, and independent committee or portfolio leadership.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Congressional and federal policy expertise: Relevant federal agricultural policy experience with Congress or federal agencies (primarily USDA and FDA), including legislative, appropriations, or regulatory policy, as well as an understanding of the roles of Congress, federal agencies, and state departments of agriculture. Relevant government affairs work in these areas is also acceptable.

  • Policy analysis and strategic judgment: Ability to track and analyze legislation, regulations, program guidance, funding proposals, and emerging issues; identify implications for states; and recommend and execute practical courses of action.

  • Advocacy and communication: Demonstrated ability to translate complex issues into concise, audience-appropriate briefs, testimony, letters, talking points, presentations, and oral advocacy.

  • Relationship building and diplomacy: Ability to establish credibility with NASDA members, congressional and government officials, partners, and coalitions; navigate differing state perspectives; and build consensus without relying on formal authority.

  • Project management: Experience managing multiple priorities, deadlines, deliverables, or related responsibilities with accuracy, accountability, and follow-through.

  • Collaboration, adaptability, and integrity: Ability to work effectively across teams, respond productively to changing priorities, learn new issues quickly, and represent NASDA with sound judgment, discretion, and nonpartisanship.

  • Education: A bachelor’s degree is required. Desired area of study in agricultural policy, food policy, political science, public policy, economics, law, or related agriculture, food, or nutrition field. An advanced degree may substitute for a portion of relevant experience where appropriate.

WORK SCHEDULE

This is a full-time (40hrs/week), exempt position at the NASDA headquarters at 4350 N Fairfax Drive, Arlington, VA. We offer a hybrid work schedule, with three days in the office and two days working from home. Working hours are generally Monday - Friday, 9 am - 5 pm local time.

Benefits:

  • PTO for vacation, sick leave, and volunteer hours

  • Tuition reimbursement

  • Professional development

  • 401k - 100% match up to 4%

The hiring range is $65,000 - $100,000 annually based on experience.

Applications without a cover letter and resume will not be considered. We look forward to meeting you!

item.title: R&D Associate in Economics at Oak Ridge National Laboratory
item.description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is the largest US Department of Energy (DOE) science and energy laboratory, conducting basic and applied research to deliver transformative solutions to compelling problems in energy and security.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is the largest US Department of Energy (DOE) science and energy laboratory, conducting basic and applied research to deliver transformative solutions to compelling problems in energy and security. Within ORNL, the Integrated Building Deployment and Analysis (IBDA) Group. The IBDA group works to optimize the energy performance of residential and commercial buildings and residential weatherization programs through applied research, technical assistance, technology deployment, and program evaluations.

The IBDA Group, in partnership with the University of Tennessee-Oak Ridge Innovation Institute (UT-ORII), is seeking an early career economist to contribute to groundbreaking research on building construction with the goals of lessening the shortage in skilled labor, increasing productivity, improving quality, enhancing safety, and lowering cost. As an ORNL staff member, the successful applicant will be part of a team of ORNL researchers and university research faculty in a UT-ORII Convergent Research Initiative focused on the development of state-of-the-art technologies for affordable manufacturing of energy-efficient, resilient buildings. In addition to being an ORNL staff member, since this role will be aligned with a UT-ORII convergent research initiative, you will also be considered a UT-ORII Fellow.

As an ORNL staff member and UT-ORII fellow, your career will develop in collaboration with researchers from both UT and ORNL through this early-career position at ORNL and with a Joint-Research Faculty (JFO) appointment at UT. As an integral part of the team, you will engage in a dynamic blend of activities. In addition to helping shape research programs, mentorship will be a key aspect of your role, guiding and inspiring graduate and undergraduate students. As a valued, early career researcher in both the ORNL Buildings and Transportation Science Directorate and UT-ORII, you’ll have access to a rich network of resources, including seminars, training opportunities, and collaborations that will propel your career forward.

We are seeking an R&D Associate in Economics with a strong interest in identifying the key factors that are increasing the cost of construction and the technologies, markets and workforce that need to be developed to attain affordable buildings. Short-term goals are to identify minimal to moderate modifications to existing technologies or approaches that the construction industry is likely to be willing to adopt. Long-term goals will define major technical opportunities that the UT-ORII fellows from multidisciplinary backgrounds should tackle.

More About UT-ORII:

The University of Tennessee-Oak Ridge Innovation Institute is a partnership of Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) and UT created to prepare interdisciplinary leaders in energy, science, and technology and develop a world-class workforce for industry, government, and academia that will drive innovation and create the industries of the future. More information is available at University of Tennessee - Oak Ridge Innovation Institute (utorii.com). Today’s energy economy is driven by disruptive technologies and swift change. The US is in a global competition for jobs, talent, and investment. To successfully compete, we must develop leadership talent in research and development (R&D), encourage entrepreneurship, and create an educational environment that promotes rapid innovation and attracts skilled professionals. Leveraging a 75-plus-year UT-ORNL partnership, UT and ORNL have developed joint institutes, joint facilities, interdisciplinary PhD programs, and comprehensive joint faculty arrangements, including 17 Governor’s Chairs recruited for the significance of their impacts in their fields. UT-ORII’s overall goal is to become a center for convergent research and talent development, helping maintain US prominence as a global innovation leader and providing tangible benefits to Tennessee.

Major Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Conduct research on technologies needed to make new building construction and retrofits of existing buildings affordable, energy efficient, and resilient.

  • Collaborate in multidisciplinary teams.

  • Development and implementation of techno economic analysis.

  • Interact and collaborate with researchers from universities, national laboratories, and private industry.

  • Present research results to ORNL staff, DOE, industry, and academia in the form of invited talks, conference papers, and peer-reviewed journal papers with high impact factors.

  • Contribute to the development of ideas and the assembly of proposals relevant to the UT-ORII Convergent Research Initiative.

  • Ensure compliance with environmental, safety, health, and program requirements.

  • Maintain a strong commitment to the implementation and continuation of ORNL’s core values and ethics.

  • Deliver ORNL’s mission by aligning behaviors, priorities, and interactions with our core values of Impact, Integrity, Teamwork, Safety, and Service. Promote equal opportunity by fostering a respectful workplace – in how we treat one another, work together, and measure success.

Basic Qualifications:

  • A Ph.D. in economics with background in building technologies assessments and affordability.

  • At least 2 years of relevant work experience.

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.

  • Strong interpersonal skills to support team building.

  • Ability to work and demonstrate critical thinking individually and as part of a diverse team.

  • Ability to develop and/or maintain strong relationships through active participation in professional societies.

  • Motivated self-starter with the ability to work independently and to participate creatively in collaborative teams across the laboratory.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong, proven publication record in the assessment of building technologies.

  • Ability to function well in a fast-paced research environment, set priorities to accomplish multiple tasks within deadlines, and adapt to ever changing needs.

  • Familiarity with DOE’s State and Community Energy Programs (SCEP).

Special Requirements:

  • For employment at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), a Real ID compliant form of identification will be required. Additionally, ORNL is subject to Department of Energy (DOE) access restrictions. All employees must also be able to obtain and maintain a federal Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card as mandated by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which requires a favorable post-employment background investigation.

  • To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete and pass a Federal Tier 1 background check investigation. This investigation includes a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last year. This includes marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws

  • For foreign national candidates: If you have not resided in the U.S. for three consecutive years, you are not eligible for the PIV credential and instead will need to obtain a favorable Local Site Specific Only (LSSO) risk determination to maintain employment. Once you meet the three-year residency requirement, you will be required to obtain a PIV credential to maintain employment.

Please submit two letters of recommendation when applying to this position. You may upload these directly to your application or have them sent to ORNLRecruiting@Ornl.gov with the position title and number referenced in the subject line.

As a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Science national laboratory, ORNL has an impressive 80-year legacy of addressing the nation’s most pressing challenges. Our team is made up of over 7,000 dedicated and innovative individuals! Our goal is to create an environment where a variety of perspectives and backgrounds are valued, ensuring ORNL is known as a top choice for employment. item.title: Junior Fiscal Policy Researcher at Institute for Economic Justice (South Africa)
item.description: The Junior Researcher will undertake research and advocacy to advance the realisation of rights through the mobilisation of resources for fiscal justice in South Africa and Africa.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Junior Researcher will undertake research and advocacy to advance the realisation of rights through the mobilisation of resources for fiscal justice in South Africa and Africa.

Working within the Resourcing for Rights Realisation (RRR) team, the Junior Researcher will contribute to policy-focused research, produce research outputs and support the development of evidence-based policy alternatives. The role will focus particularly on fiscal policy, taxation, public expenditure, progressive revenue mobilisation and IEJ’s work on South Africa’s state of the national address (SONA), national budget, and Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS).

The role will also involve engaging with partners and stakeholders to advance research findings and policy alternatives, while contributing to the broader RRR team’s work on budget justice, macroeconomic policy, and climate finance where these intersect with fiscal policy.

Examples of key publications from this workstream can be found here, here, and here.

ABOUT YOU

You are someone who:

  • Has strong political and social awareness or consciousness.

  • Is committed to and understands economic and social justice.

  • Is able to work independently, take initiative, and demonstrate accountability for delivering high-quality outputs.

  • Is organised and detail-oriented.

  • Has the ability to exercise sound judgement and make well-reasoned decisions.

  • Has strong interpersonal awareness and emotional intelligence in engaging with colleagues and stakeholders.

  • Is comfortable working in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

  • Can communicate complex ideas clearly to a range of audiences.

  • Has strong verbal and written communication skills.

  • Is proficient using Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace.

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

Fiscal policy research

  • Conduct and contribute to high-quality, policy-focused research outputs and publications, taking responsibility for agreed research outputs.

  • Undertake rigorous research on relevant fiscal policy themes, including taxation, public expenditure and progressive domestic revenue mobilisation.

  • Contribute to research concept notes, working papers, policy briefs and submissions on tax, expenditure, domestic revenue mobilisation and budget proposals.

  • Collect, analyse and interpret economic and fiscal data to inform research findings and policy recommendations.

  • Support the commissioning, coordination and review of research outputs produced by consultants.

  • Participate in and organise research forums, workshops, and knowledge-sharing platforms.

  • Review, comment on, and contribute to research outputs across IEJ.

Fiscal justice advocacy and public engagement

  • Contribute to IEJ’s research and advocacy activities on South Africa’s national budget and MTBPS, including pre- and post-budget analysis, statements and parliamentary submissions, taking responsibility for agreed advocacy outputs with appropriate guidance and support.

  • Plan and organise advocacy activities informed by research findings, and contribute to the development and implementation of advocacy strategies in collaboration with RRR, IEJ teams, and partners.

  • Develop accessible summaries and advocacy materials, including opinion pieces, policy briefs, and other communications based on research and policy work.

  • Contribute to advocacy efforts towards budget justice and social security for all, including participation in the Budget Justice Coalition’s (BJC) fiscal policy work.

  • Engage with policymakers, government, labour, and civil society partners on fiscal policy matters, and contribute to relevant policy discussions.

  • Participate in media engagements and represent IEJ in relevant forums with appropriate support and guidance.

Process and stakeholder relationship management

  • Contribute to building and maintaining partnerships within the fiscal policy space, both locally and internationally, including relationships with IEJ’s strategic partners.

  • Support the preparation and coordination of submissions to institutions such as government, Parliament, NEDLAC, UN bodies and the African Union (AU).

  • Coordinate and/or participate in relevant tax and fiscal policy working forums.

  • Contribute to donor reporting and funding processes where required.

  • Support the development of proposals for funding opportunities.

Team contribution and development

  • Take responsibility for assigned research and advocacy outputs, including planning work, meeting deadlines, and communicating progress.

  • Support the Senior Researcher and other team members on cross-cutting work.

  • Contribute to project planning, budgeting, implementation, and reporting processes.

  • Collaborate across IEJ teams to support budget advocacy and related initiatives.

  • Develop greater independence in fiscal policy research, budget analysis, policy writing and stakeholder engagement through practical experience, feedback and technical support.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • A completed Master’s degree in Economics, Development, Social Sciences, or related fields (e.g., Sociology, Political Science, or Public Policy). Candidates currently completing a Masters degree may be considered where they demonstrate relevant research and policy experience.

  • A minimum of one year’s relevant research experience, with strong qualitative and quantitative research skills, including the ability to analyse and interpret economic and fiscal data. Experience in economic modelling is essential.

  • Experience working with various stakeholders across civil society, public policy, government, or research environments.

  • Strong writing and analytical skills, with the ability to produce high-quality, policy-relevant outputs.

  • Strong verbal and presentation skills, with media experience as an added bonus.

  • Understanding of the policy debates in the fiscal and macroeconomic policy and economic justice spaces, with the ability to develop and communicate clear, well-structured arguments across a range of platforms, including the media.

  • Ability to work independently, take initiative, and manage multiple priorities.

  • Sound judgement and the ability to make well-reasoned decisions.

  • Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence in engaging with colleagues and stakeholders.

  • Flexibility and ability to work in a fast-paced environment.

ABOUT THE RESOURCING FOR RIGHTS REALISATION PROJECT

The RRR project seeks the adoption by African governments of policies that mobilise the maximum available domestic and international resources in an equitable and transparent manner to invest in the realisation of socio-economic rights and planetary wellbeing, including through a more just integration in a fairer and more democratic global financial system. The project focuses on four areas: 1. Macroeconomic policy; 2. Fiscal policy; 3. Fiscal governance, transparency and accountability; 4. International Financial Institutions (IFIs); and 5. Climate finance that advances a just transition.

CONTRACT

The contract will be a full-time 3-year contract, beginning as soon as possible.

SALARY (TCTC)

The IEJ’s new Remuneration Policy sets the Researcher salary range at R435 253 – R572 701, depending on experience. Salaries are reviewed annually in line with cost-of-living adjustments and performance.

LOCATION

The position is based in Braamfontein, Johannesburg. The IEJ currently operates on a hybrid work model, with in-office days currently on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. This may change in the future.

The IEJ is committed to gender and racial equity and transformation and will consider this when reviewing applications.

Posted Job Title

Job Profile Title

Research Specialist C

Job Description Summary

The Water Center Research Specialist, reporting to the Director of Applied Research and Policy, will play a central role in leading and executing the Center’s applied research and policy initiatives. This position is responsible for designing and advancing research projects, producing high-impact analytical and communications deliverables, and translating complex water infrastructure and policy issues into actionable insights for diverse stakeholders. The Specialist will work closely with Water Center staff and collaborators across Penn to drive interdisciplinary efforts and extend the reach and impact of the Center’s work. Graduate-level training or equivalent subject matter expertise in environmental policy, water resources, or environmental studies is required. This is a hybrid position, with an expectation of three days per week in the Water Center offices.

Job Description

The Water Center at Penn is a community focused research center working to find integrated solutions to the challenges facing water systems and watersheds. We strive to be a trusted, reliable partner whose work accelerates water equity.

DUTIES:

Lead applied research projects from design to delivery, including writing reports, developing surveys and interviews, creating public-facing materials, and presenting to stakeholders.

Conduct research on water infrastructure technical assistance and emerging water policy challenges by collecting, analyzing, and interpreting data and evaluating relevant policies across drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater systems.

Conduct research on emerging contaminant policy by collecting, analyzing, and interpreting data and evaluating the impacts of existing policies.

Collaborate with the Communications Manager, Penn partners, and external stakeholders, including utilities, government agencies, and nonprofit organizations, to translate research into strategic communications, inform policy and practice, and support interdisciplinary initiatives.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s degree and 3 to 5 years of experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience, is required. A Master’s degree is preferred. Should have education or experience in environmental policy, water resources, environmental studies, environmental engineering and/or water system management.

Experience conducting applied research, including designing surveys or interviews, analyzing qualitative and quantitative data, and synthesizing findings to inform policy or technical assistance.

item.description: This Senior Applied Research Economist position combines applied economic research with leadership of the Early Warning System of Farm Financial Stress (EWS).
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
This Senior Applied Research Economist position combines applied economic research with leadership of the Early Warning System of Farm Financial Stress (EWS). This role will advance RaFF’s research and stakeholder engagement activities focused on farm financial conditions, agricultural lending, and financial stress in the farm sector.

The role develops analytical tools and models, conducts applied research on farm finance and agricultural credit markets, and leads EWS activities across participating states. Working with producers, lenders, policymakers, researchers, and Extension professionals, the position integrates economic analysis and stakeholder intelligence to identify emerging risks and deliver actionable insights that support decision-making across the agricultural finance sector.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the implementation and improvement of the Early Warning System of Farm Financial Stress (EWS).

  • Engage producers, lenders, Extension professionals, researchers, policymakers, and other stakeholders to monitor emerging financial risks and conditions.

  • Coordinate EWS stakeholder meetings, manage project activities, and oversee development of consensus reports and related outputs.

  • Synthesize stakeholder input, economic data, and analytical findings into reports, presentations, and decision-support materials.

  • Develop and enhance models used for farm income projections, agricultural lending analysis, farm financial stress assessment, and policy evaluation.

  • Conduct applied research on farm finance, agricultural credit markets, and related policy issues.

  • Contribute to Farm Income Outlook reports, Missouri Agricultural Outlook publications, and other RaFF products.

  • Present findings to policymakers, producers, lenders, industry groups, and professional audiences.

  • Lead collaborative projects and pursue external funding opportunities that support RaFF’s mission.

  • Mentor graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and research staff as appropriate.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

  • Knowledge of U.S. agricultural policy, commodity markets, farm finance, and agricultural lending.

  • Experience conducting applied economic analysis and developing decision-support tools.

  • Ability to integrate quantitative analysis with stakeholder input to assess emerging conditions and risks.

  • Experience leading collaborative projects and stakeholder engagement activities.

  • Quality and impact of applied research, policy analysis, reports, and presentations.

  • Strong written and oral communication skills for technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Experience with applied economic modeling, econometrics, forecasting, or policy analysis.

  • Experience leading stakeholder engagement, consensus-building processes, or multi-state initiatives.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Washington’s Housing Futures Center in the College of Built Environments has an outstanding opportunity for a Housing Researcher (Research Scientist/Engineer 4 (E S UAW Research) to join their team.

About this Opportunity

The Housing Researcher will serve as the primary staff researcher for the Housing Futures Center and will support all housing-related research initiatives within the Center. Working closely with the Center Director and in partnership with faculty and researchers across the University of Washington, the Housing Researcher manages interdisciplinary research projects, supports efforts to secure external research funding, disseminates research findings, and advances evidence-based housing policy and practice. The role supports the Center’s mission to improve housing outcomes through rigorous research, community engagement, and policy impact.

The Housing Researcher will advance the University’s research mission by leading externally funded housing research programs and producing high-impact scholarly and policy-relevant research. The position contributes to the University’s reputation as a leader in housing research, supports interdisciplinary collaboration, and expands engagement with governmental, nonprofit, philanthropic, and community partners. Research findings inform housing policy and practice affecting communities across Washington State and beyond.

This position requires leadership of multiple complex research initiatives involving diverse stakeholders, funding sources, and methodological approaches. The holder of this position must lead multiple research projects, manage research funding, support efforts to secure external funding, manage competing project priorities, balance academic rigor with community needs, and effectively communicate findings to both scholarly and non-technical audiences. Success requires substantial expertise in housing research, stakeholder engagement, and project management.

About This Team

The Housing Futures Center at the University of Washington’s College of Built Environments is a bold, forward-looking initiative designed to address Washington’s most pressing housing challenges, both today and in the years ahead. The Center builds capacity and advances informed decision-making by integrating research, education, and community engagement to support policymakers, advocates, developers, housing providers, tenants, and homeowners in shaping a future where every Washingtonian has access to housing.

Key Responsibilities

25% – Research Leadership and Program Development

· Support strategic leadership for the Housing Futures Center’s research agenda.

· Support the development and execution of complex, multidisciplinary housing research projects.

· Ensure scientific rigor, methodological excellence, and high-quality research outputs.

· Identify emerging research opportunities and develop innovative research initiatives aligned with the Center’s mission.

· Manage research timelines, deliverables, and project priorities across multiple concurrent initiatives.

35% - Research execution and dissemination

· Design and oversee quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods research studies, with a particular emphasis on applied research.

· Author and co-author peer-reviewed journal articles, policy briefs, technical reports, and other scholarly products.

· Present research findings at academic conferences, public forums, and stakeholder meetings.

· Translate research findings into accessible products that inform policy and practice.

15% - Support efforts to secure research funding

· Support the development of competitive grant proposals to public agencies, foundations, and other funding organizations.

· Collaborate with faculty investigators and external partners to secure research funding.

15% – Strategic Partnerships and External Engagement

· Cultivate and maintain partnerships with government agencies, community organizations, nonprofit organizations, and philanthropic partners.

· Represent the Housing Futures Center in regional and national collaborations.

· Identify opportunities for research that informs evidence-based housing policy and practice.

· Support the Center’s efforts to increase its visibility and impact among policymakers, practitioners, and academic audiences.

10% – Mentorship and Research Capacity Building

· Mentor research staff, graduate students, postdoctoral scholars, and affiliated researchers.

· Provide guidance on research methodology, study design, data analysis, and scholarly dissemination.

· Foster a collaborative research environment that supports interdisciplinary inquiry and innovation.

· Contribute to the development of research infrastructure, systems, and best practices within the Center.

Position Qualifications

To be considered for this opportunity, your application must demonstrate that you meet both the minimum qualifications and additional qualifications listed below. Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

Minimum Qualifications

· Master’s degree in urban planning, public policy, sociology, economics, geography, social work, public health, or a closely related field.

· A minimum of four years of progressively responsible research experience in an academic, policy, government, or research organization setting, broadly related to housing, which could include housing policy, housing markets, housing development, homelessness, housing affordability, community development, or closely related areas.

Applicants who do not meet these qualifications WILL NOT be forwarded to the Hiring Manager.

Additional Qualifications

· Demonstrated training in both quantitative and qualitative research methods, including mixed methods approaches. Experience conducting research with quantitative data and analysis is required.

· Record of a growing research agenda, including scholarly publications, policy reports, and public dissemination of research findings.

· Experience leading or supporting complex research projects and managing multiple priorities simultaneously.

· Experience in grant writing and research funding development.

· Experience collaborating with community organizations, public agencies, and other external stakeholders.

· Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

· Ability to communicate research findings effectively to both academic and non-academic audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

· PhD or equivalent doctoral degree in urban planning, public policy, sociology, economics, geography, social work, public health, or a closely related field.

· Established national or regional reputation in housing research.

· Experience conducting applied research related to housing instability, homelessness, affordable housing, or housing systems.

· Experience supervising research staff and mentoring graduate students or early-career researchers.

· Experience with a range of research methods and demonstrated expertise in one or more of the following: working with large administrative datasets, survey research, a range of quantitative methods, qualitative research, and community-engaged research methods.

item.content:encoded:
This is a three year-term position with the possibility of extension based on funding and organizational needs. The salary range for this position is $61,000 to $72,000

ORGANIZATION OVERVIEW

As a strategic partner of the United Nations, the United Nations Foundation brings together fresh thinking and diverse voices around innovative ideas to drive progress and tackle problems. Sometimes we work behind-the-scenes, shaping negotiations and connecting experts, advocates and decision-makers. Other times we drive public awareness and involvement through communications, campaigns, and convenings. Over the years we’ve developed a diverse and dynamic portfolio of capabilities, tools, and platforms to help the UN build a better world for everyone, everywhere.

The Global Partnership for Sustainable Development Data (the Global Partnership), an alliance hosted at the UN Foundation, is a fast-growing, dynamic international partnership bringing together over 700 different organizations including governments, UN agencies, private companies, civil society organizations, and many others. We make connections and broker partnerships to address the problems of gaps in data production, poor data use, access, quality, and to work with stakeholders to fully harness the new opportunities of the data revolution in the service of sustainable development. We aim to link and align action, capacities and resources across geographies, sectors and data communities.

JOB SUMMARY

Reporting to the Senior Director of Operations, and in close coordination with the Agriculture Program Lead, the Manager will support the Global Partnership’s thematic engagements on agriculture data. This includes working with the Global Partnership’s Regional Leads to strengthen agriculture and food security data systems in Global Partnership countries and coordinating advocacy related to country work in Rome, where the UN’s food agencies are headquartered. They will develop and maintain strong trusted relationships with government representatives and Global Partnership partners from all regions, with a strong focus on West Africa. The Manager will also develop and contribute to knowledge products that aim to shape key stakeholders’ view of the importance of agricultural data, the need to strengthen data systems and capacities, and how to achieve that.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Country Duties

  • Develop strong relationships with government partners at the country-level in National Statistical Offices, Ministries of Agriculture and other entities to understand their data needs, identify ways to strengthen data systems, and promote data use and sharing in the food and agriculture sector

  • Develop use cases in collaboration with government partners and provide advice and assistance on their implementation

  • Engage with select political and technical partners to identify opportunities for their engagement in support of country level implementation on agricultural data

  • Develop and organize various meetings, seminars, events and roundtables that aim to address issues related to the gap in agricultural data, and data use and sharing

  • Procure and manage consultants engaged to assist with the work

Advocacy

  • Provide support for the Global Partnership’s activities related to advocacy in Rome, where the UN’s food agencies are headquartered, by:

    • Understanding the political landscape and helping to implement the strategy for stakeholder engagement and influence in Rome;

    • Building relationships with member state representatives and other stakeholders in Rome;

    • Assisting with the management of consultants; and,

    • Assist with the coordination of meetings and events

  • Engage at regional and global levels to support the Global Partnership’s strategy on agricultural data, in diverse areas spanning official and non-official data communities

  • Develop and contribute to various knowledge products that make the case for investing in agriculture data and statistics, improving data governance and data sharing, leveraging concrete country examples, and linking to related global policy processes

Other Duties

  • Develop and maintain an understanding of the dynamics and key issues on data for development and identify how these may affect or help strengthen agricultural data

  • Liaise with key donors and program partners in the agriculture sector to build and maintain new funding and project relationships

  • Coordinate closely with the Communications team and MEL Manager to capture impact stories, results and lessons from country and Rome-based work, and contribute content that supports the Global Partnership’s communications and reporting efforts

  • Other duties as assigned

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Agricultural Data Manager is not a supervisory role.

EDUCATION/CERTIFICATION and/or EXPERIENCE

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.

  • Bachelors’ degree in international development, public policy, agricultural development or related field or commensurate years of experience

  • 5-7 years of related work experience

  • Knowledge of data-related issues in the agriculture sector

  • Knowledge of intergovernmental data sharing best practices preferred

  • Familiarity with the 50x2030 Initiative preferred

  • Proficiency in French and English required

  • Understanding of Rome-based agencies’ governance and budgeting processes preferred

  • Experience in data for development and financing for data preferred

  • Project management experience preferred

SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the required skills and competencies.

  • Demonstrated ability to take ownership of responsibilities, follow through on commitments, and consistently deliver high-quality results with integrity and reliability

  • Ability to collaborate effectively across teams, functions, and diverse perspectives to foster productive working relationships and achieve shared organizational goals

  • Strong critical thinking and sound judgment, with the ability to evaluate information, exercise discretion, anticipate challenges, and make informed decisions in complex or evolving situations

  • Strong organizational and project management skills, including the ability to prioritize competing demands, coordinate resources, manage timelines, and deliver results within established deadlines

  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders, communicate clearly, manage expectations, and navigate competing priorities to achieve desired outcomes

  • Ability to apply relevant technical, functional, and professional expertise to solve problems, inform decisions, implement effective solutions, and continuously improve work practices

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The essential functions of this role will generally be performed in a remote work environment, provided the employee maintains a dedicated workspace that supports confidentiality and productivity. Remote employees must ensure limited background noise and environmental distractions to effectively perform essential job functions

This role will also travel frequently, with approximately 6 trips per year of 1 to 2 weeks duration each.

LOCATION

This role must be based in Rome, Italy, or Abuja / Lagos, Nigeria. Applicants located in Nigeria must have or be able to secure a Schengen visa in order to travel to Rome as needed.

DISABILITY SPECIFICATIONS

  • dental insurance

  • back-up care

Additionally, all benefit eligible employees have 12 paid holidays, 20 vacation days, 10 sick days, 3 personal days, and 8 weeks of family leave care.

item.title: Gas Utility Decarbonization Strategy Manager at ICF
item.description: You will be a key member of a client facing consulting team within ICF’s Energy and Climate Planning Line of Business (LOB).
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
You will be a key member of a client facing consulting team within ICF’s Energy and Climate Planning Line of Business (LOB). Your specific team is focused on supporting gas and combined gas-electric utilities with strategy and planning related to decarbonization, but you will collaborate with a wide range of teams across relevant energy and decarbonization topics.

You will be primarily responsible for leading projects and managing staff to deliver solutions to identified client problems, including review and presentation of analytical findings. You will lead teams that use a variety of analytical and modeling techniques to assess and forecast potential decarbonization impacts on utility customers, utility infrastructure, costs, and GHG emissions, in order to provide insights that support gas utility strategic planning and regulatory efforts. You will also be responsible for building and maintaining client relationships and supporting sales and business development efforts.

Your work will play a critical role in helping natural gas utilities, combined utilities, governments, and other clients prepare for and adapt to changing market, technology, and policy conditions over the coming years. The team performs a wide range of decarbonization related work for utilities, and candidates with relevant natural gas utility decarbonization experience in a range of different areas are encouraged to apply. This position is formally posted as a Hybrid position under the location of ICF’s headquarters (Reston, VA), but ICF will also consider candidates based in other regions in the US or Canada (including remote work in areas where the Company does not have offices).

Key Responsibilities:

  • Work with clients and manage engagements to tackle complex challenges related to the role of gas utilities in supporting energy and decarbonization targets and policies.

  • Lead teams that perform quantitative and economic analyses of decarbonization pathways and energy and climate policies, with a focus on impacts and opportunities for gas utilities, to assess and forecast future technology adoption, fuel and power consumption, utility infrastructure impacts, cost impacts, customer rate impacts, emissions reductions, and implementation and regulatory challenges.

  • Manage and grow client relationships by delivering excellent value, consistency, quality, and dependability.

  • Support sales and business development efforts with market research, outreach, proposal development, and thought leadership.

  • Collaborate and communicate effectively with other ICF and client teams.

  • Mentor and provide direction to junior staff in the course of their work.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • A bachelor’s degree in the fields of engineering, energy policy, business, or economics.

  • 8+ years of work experience related to analysis, policy, and/or regulations related to natural gas demand, gas infrastructure, energy efficiency, and/or decarbonization.

  • Experience working with natural gas or electric utilities

  • Project management experience.

Preferred Skills/Experience:

  • 12+ years of work experience related to analysis, policy, and/or regulations related to natural gas demand, gas infrastructure, energy efficiency, and/or decarbonization

  • Experience working at a natural gas utility

  • Experience with utility regulatory proceedings

  • Consulting experience

  • Master’s degree in the fields of engineering, energy policy, business, or economics

  • Client management and/or business development experience

  • Specialized knowledge of opportunities related to the decarbonization of gas utilities, potentially including energy efficiency, non-pipeline alternatives, methane emission reductions, renewable natural gas, hydrogen, and/or heat pumps

  • Strong analytical aptitude

  • Strong communication and writing skills

Working at ICF

ICF is a global advisory and technology services provider, but we’re not your typical consultants. We combine unmatched expertise with cutting-edge technology to help clients solve their most complex challenges, navigate change, and shape the future.

We can only solve the world’s toughest challenges by building a workplace that allows everyone to thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer. Together, our employees are empowered to share their expertise and collaborate with others to achieve personal and professional goals. For more information, please read our EEO policy.

We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Candidates who currently hold valid work authorization may be considered for a change of employer petition, subject to company policy and applicable immigration requirements.

To request an accommodation, please email Candidateaccommodation@icf.com and we will be happy to assist. All information you provide will be kept confidential and will be used only to the extent required to provide needed reasonable accommodations. 

Read more about workplace discrimination rights or our benefit offerings which are included in the Transparency in (Benefits) Coverage Act.

Applicants needing an accommodation for disability or religious purposes in connection with the application process should contact Candidateaccommodation@icf.com for assistance.

item.content:encoded:
FTC economists make independent policy recommendations to the Commission based on their theoretical and empirical analysis of relevant issues. Research by FTC economists is supported and encouraged, in part through the Bureau’s working paper series, seminar series, and annual FTC Microeconomics Conference. FTC economists regularly present their work at seminars/conferences, and publish in top journals. Economists in all fields of applied microeconomics and econometrics are encouraged to apply.

Duties

As an Economist at the Federal Trade Commission you will perform the following duties:

  • Apply statistical, mathematical, and econometric techniques to the analysis of data to empirically analyze economic theories and test hypotheses in support of policy recommendations.

  • Provide analysis and interpretation of economic and related information collected from companies to support policy and program decision-making.

  • Identify and collect the appropriate data needed to analyze the validity of competing economic theories.

  • Conduct investigations, reviews, and studies that apply a thorough knowledge of microeconomic theory to study the behavior of individual consumers, firms, and industries in order to analyze how markets establish relative prices among goods and services and thereby allocate limited resources among alternative uses.

  • Analyze the likely effects on consumers and firm competition of mergers, agreements between firms, and individual firm business practices.

  • Prepare economic impact assessments under the laws that govern federal rulemaking to ensure adequate considerations of the costs and benefits of proposed rules.

  • Develop oral and written products, tailored to the needs of the audience, in support of recommendations involving issues such as the economic aspects of new or proposed investigations, policies, or rules affecting FTC programs.

  • Undertake research aimed at addressing unresolved theoretical or empirical questions in topics related to competition, consumer protection, and general understanding of consumer and firm behavior.

  • Draft, present, and defend positions for policy, enforcement decisions, and education of other competition and consumer protection agencies.
