item.description: At the World Bank, a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
At the World Bank, a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/who-we-are/ibrd

About the Global Environment Facility (GEF)

The Global Environment Facility (GEF) is a family of funds dedicated to confronting biodiversity loss, climate change, pollution, and strains on land and ocean health. Its grants, blended financing, and policy support help developing countries address their biggest environmental priorities and adhere to international environmental conventions. Over the past three decades, the GEF has provided more than $23 billion and mobilized $129 billion in co-financing for more than 5,000 national and regional projects.

The GEF unites 186 countries in partnership with international institutions, civil society organizations, Indigenous Peoples, and the private sector to address global environmental issues while supporting national sustainable development initiatives. An independently operating financial organization, the GEF serves as a financial mechanism for six major Multilateral Environmental Agreements (MEAs), including the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The GEF Secretariat, construed for administrative purposes as a Vice-Presidential Unit (VPU) within the World Bank, has approximately 100 professional and administrative and client support (ACS) staff.

About the LDCF and SCCF

The Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF) and the Special Climate Change Fund (SCCF) are two dedicated financial mechanisms established under the UNFCCC and managed by the GEF. As part of the GEF family of funds, the LDCF and SCCF play a critical role in supporting developing countries, particularly least developed countries (LDCs) and small island developing States (SIDS), in building resilience to climate change impacts and implementing priority adaptation actions identified in National Adaptation Programmes of Action (NAPAs) and National Adaptation Plans (NAPs).

The LDCF and SCCF operate on the basis of voluntary donor contributions, which have historically been replenished through pledging meetings held in conjunction with GEF Council meetings, UNFCCC Conferences of the Parties (COPs), and/or other major events. Since their inception, the funds have received contributions from 28 donor countries and work with a voluntary contribution model, based on agreed four-year financial scenarios for the two funds.

The role will seek to advance multi-year pledging mechanisms, improved coordination among donors, clearer strategic positioning of the funds’ comparative advantages within the climate finance architecture, and proactive engagement with potential new contributors. A central aim is to broaden and diversify the contributor base beyond traditional sovereign donors to include sub-national governments, philanthropies, and private sector actors, while using blended and innovative finance instruments to catalyze additional investment in climate adaptation.

Role Summary:

The GEF Secretariat is seeking an experienced Senior Resource Mobilization Specialist to join the GEF Division on MEAs and Funds to coordinate LDCF and SCCF resource mobilization and partnership building, enabling timely and effective programming in developing countries to address their climate adaptation priorities under the UNFCCC. The role is also expected to make contributions towards the development and implementation of a resource mobilization strategy for the GEF family of funds.

The ideal candidate should have a strong understanding of the climate adaptation finance landscape, innovative financing opportunities, and the dynamics of GEF client countries. The candidate should possess strong interpersonal skills, demonstrated experience with climate finance resource mobilization, along with political acumen and the capacity to work effectively on sensitive issues with senior management, the GEF Council, LDCF/SCCF contributors, and across different agencies of the GEF.

The Senior Specialist will play an instrumental role in mobilizing resources and related strategic planning by developing and facilitating effective partnerships with confirmed and potential contributors to the LDCF and SCCF, including donor governments, philanthropic organizations, private sector actors, foundations, non-governmental organizations, sub-national governments, and bilateral and multilateral institutions.

Key Duties and Accountabilities

Under the supervision of the Manager of the GEF MEAs and Funds Division, the Senior Resource Mobilization Specialist for the LDCF and SCCF will have the following duties:

• Coordinate resource mobilization for the LDCF and SCCF by articulating resource mobilization needs; organizing partnership building and fundraising efforts and supporting engagement of GEF management; and monitoring and tracking progress against targets. Engage with all sources of support, including sovereign and sub-national governments, philanthropic organizations, private sector, foundations, non-governmental organizations, and bilateral and multilateral institutions, in addition to innovative sources of financing.
• Enhance synergies across the GEF family of funds by contributing to GEF-wide resource mobilization efforts and external engagement, and by helping to articulate a unique value proposition for the LDCF and SCCF within the broader climate • Develop and implement a forward-looking resource mobilization strategy, including segmented donor engagement strategies for traditional donors, emerging economy donors, private sector actors, and philanthropic foundations; specific, time-bound resource mobilization targets and milestones; mechanisms to strengthen predictability and planning security; and proposals for innovative financing instruments, including blended finance windows, co-financing frameworks, and impact investment mechanisms.
• Prepare documents and briefing materials to inform resource mobilization discussions for the GEF Council and GEF management. Contribute to GEF Council organization and discussions on matters related to LDCF/SCCF resource mobilization and organize outreach and visibility enhancement efforts in coordination with the Communications team, including the development of donor-facing investment case documents, infographics, and digital communications materials.
• Analyze priorities, operational modalities, and other requirements of potential contributors and support sources, and articulate responses that take into consideration LDCF/SCCF governance arrangements and policies. Support the design, external engagement and operationalization of arrangements to facilitate new and non-sovereign contributions.
• Conduct diagnostic assessments of the LDCF and SCCF resource mobilization landscape, including historical contribution trends, donor engagement patterns, funding gaps, and emerging opportunities. Benchmark LDCF/SCCF approaches against comparable multilateral funds to identify positioning opportunities and transferable lessons.
• Design and facilitate structured stakeholder consultation processes and external engagement, including multi-stakeholder workshops with donor governments, recipient country representatives, GEF Secretariat staff, and civil society organizations, as well as bilateral consultations with key donor government representatives.
• Collaborate with relevant teams, including the Policy and Operations Division regarding resource mobilization-related considerations, and the World Bank Trustee team on contributions and due diligence processes. Ensure cross-cutting considerations including gender equality, social inclusion, indigenous peoples’ rights, and the needs of the most climate-vulnerable communities are integrated throughout.
• Provide backstopping to GEF management and carry out additional technical and policy-relevant tasks as assigned.

Selection Criteria

• Master’s degree or Ph.D. in the field of climate finance, environmental finance, development finance, international development, economics, public policy, or any other relevant discipline.
• At least 8 years of progressively responsible professional experience in resource mobilization, climate finance, development finance, or international partnerships management, with a demonstrated track record in developing and implementing resource mobilization or fundraising strategies for multilateral organizations, international NGOs, or development finance institutions. Knowledge of innovative and blended finance mechanisms is required.
• Demonstrated experience working with or supporting GEF-managed funds, including the LDCF, SCCF, or comparable multilateral climate funds, is strongly preferred.
• Familiarity with the UNFCCC climate finance architecture, including the roles of other climate funds, bilateral climate funds, and MDB climate finance windows, as well as relevant UNFCCC negotiations and decisions related to adaptation finance.
• Experience in strategic interactions with sovereign and non-sovereign contributors, including donor government representatives at senior levels in the context of pledging conferences or replenishment negotiations, private and institutional investors, foundations, sub-national governments, and other entities, is highly desirable.
• Ability to think analytically, strategically, and programmatically, with strong skills in synthesizing complex information from multiple sources into clear, actionable recommendations.
• Proven ability to work with and across teams, both as a team leader and team member, in a multicultural environment and independently on complex tasks under tight deadlines.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English, including the ability to communicate complex issues to a wide range of audiences, including non-technical stakeholders. Proficiency in French and/or Spanish is desirable, given the geographic distribution of LDCF/SCCF recipient countries.

This role provides support to a Financial Intermediary Fund (FIF). Roles funded by a FIF are subject to the WBG Staff Directives and Procedures. Additionally, the FIF’s governance framework and funding are also relevant to this role.

As the World Bank Group continues to evolve, we value candidates who:

  • Demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively across teams, disciplines, cultures, and institutional boundaries.

  • Responsibly leverage digital and AI-enabled tools to enhance productivity, learning, and decision-making.

  • Bring experience working in fragile, conflict-affected, and violent (FCV) contexts and are encouraged to highlight relevant experience in their application materials, where applicable.

WBG Culture Attributes:

1. Sense of urgency: Anticipate and quickly respond to the needs of internal and external stakeholders.
2. Thoughtful risk-taking: Challenge the status quo and push boundaries to achieve greater impact.
3. Empowerment and accountability: Empower yourself and others to act and hold each other accountable for results.

World Bank Group Core Competencies

We are proud to be an equal opportunity and inclusive employer with a dedicated and committed workforce, and do not discriminate based on gender, gender identity, religion, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or disability.

item.description: We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world.

item.content:encoded:
We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. Founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. We believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. We provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.

The Team

The Global Development (GD) Division includes a diverse range of program areas focused on finding creative ways to ensure solutions and products get into the hands of people in low-income countries. We focus on areas with the potential for high-impact, sustainable solutions that can reach millions of people. Our strategies include Emergency Response, Immunization, and Polio Eradication. A common theme across these programs is focus on innovative delivery, including an emphasis on strengthening primary health care systems. Our teams work in close partnership with Regional and Country Office Teams to align the foundation’s health and development equity agenda with the government’s broader priorities.

Within GD, the Exemplars in Global Health (EGH) program equips decision-makers with the evidence, insights, and practical “know-how” needed to accelerate and scale interventions that improve the health of the world’s most vulnerable populations. Working with a global network of partners, EGH identifies and studies exemplars and best practices across health outcomes, primary health care systems, and service delivery strategies.

Through rigorous research, evidence synthesis, and timely analysis, EGH translates lessons on what works into actionable insights that help policymakers, practitioners, and funders strengthen systems, improve service delivery, and address pressing global health challenges.

We pursue this through...
1. The study of “positive outliers”—identifying countries or regions that have achieved exceptional progress in health outcomes and analyzing the drivers behind their success;
2. The study of emerging practices with global learning value, using prospective research and real-time analytics alongside implementation to meet the ambition of ‘learning by doing’;
3. The provision of internal advisory services to support teams in pursuit of the Foundation’s three goals toward 2045; and
4. External partnerships to scale exemplary practices with governments, policymakers, global health initiatives, and multilateral development banks.

Application Deadline, Thursday, November 5, 2026

*We are hiring for two (2) Senior Program Officers for this team.

Your Role

The Senior Program Officer, Policy & Evidence will scope and create opportunities for EGH’s evidence to shape policy, program, and funding decisions, drawing on deep institutional knowledge and a policy advocacy approach to identify where and when EGH’s voice can matter most.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and lead partnership strategies with one or more global health institutions (e.g., multilateral development banks, multilateral funds or agencies) to drive uptake of EGH evidence in their policy and funding decisions, and track impact, in close coordination with relevant teams at the foundation.

  • Proactively find opportunities for new or existing research and analysis to advance EGH’s partnerships with global health institutions and advise EGH teams on how to position this work to influence policy and funding decisions.

  • Build and sustain coalitions of governments, technical partners, and institutions aligned around shared evidence-to-policy goals across global, regional, and/or national levels, in close coordination with relevant teams at the foundation.

  • Lead the development and presentation of policy briefs, position papers, and other decision-ready materials to improve use of EGH evidence by leaders at the global, regional and country level.

  • Manage consultants and contractors supporting partnerships strategies.

  • Share intelligence on institutional priorities and processes to shape upstream research design of EGH teams.

Your Experience

  • 10+ years of experience in global health policy, advocacy, or development-focused consulting; Masters or other advanced degree preferred.

  • Demonstrated success designing and implementing strategies that influence policymaking and policymakers, financiers, or ecosystem leaders.

  • Strong understanding of how LMIC governments and/or global health/development institutions and partners (e.g., World Bank/multilateral development banks, the Global Fund, Gavi, UNICEF) consume and use evidence to inform policies and programs.

  • Ability to credibly convene and influence diverse partners, filter information, frame issues, and determine what information is ready for translation into a policy priority in a dynamic environment.

  • Strong understanding of the foundation’s work from a program perspective and the global context surrounding the foundation’s initiatives.

  • Comfort with highly unstructured and ambiguous situations, with the ability to proactively bring structure and resolution.

  • Experience living and working in low- and middle-income countries preferred.

  • Excellent organizational, facilitation, oral, and written communication skills. Ability to work effectively and with sensitivity across barriers such as language, culture, and distance, with excellent listening skills and compassion.

  • Ability to work with flexibility, efficiency, diplomacy, and enthusiasm in a fast-paced environment, as a member of an integrated team.

**Must have unrestricted work authorization in the country where this position is located. The Foundation does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. This includes direct company sponsorship and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (eg: H-1B, O-1, L-1,  E, OPT, STEM-OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.).

item.title: AI Initiative Policy Fellow at Center for Global Development (US or UK)
item.description: The Center for Global Development (CGD) is an independent, non-partisan, non-profit policy research organization in Washington, DC and London, UK that focuses on the issues and institutions that are critical to inclusive development.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Center for Global Development (CGD) is an independent, non-partisan, non-profit policy research organization in Washington, DC and London, UK that focuses on the issues and institutions that are critical to inclusive development. Through rigorous empirical research and active engagement with the global policy community, we focus on the policy intersections of low- and middle-income countries and the governments, institutions, and corporations that can be partners in delivering greater progress.

The Center is seeking a Policy Fellow, based in Washington, DC or London, to help build a new Artificial Intelligence Initiative. CGD’s AI Initiative works to ensure AI’s potential delivers for the world’s poor. We are focused on three domains related to AI: (1) Effectiveness — distinguishing credible AI solutions from hype through evidence-based frameworks for evaluation, procurement, and scaling decisions; (2) Access — extending AI’s benefits to underserved LMIC populations despite gaps in connectivity, devices, and language support; and (3) Transformation — preparing LMICs for a world where AI can perform most economically valuable digital tasks, and the policies, infrastructure, and institutions needed to navigate that shift.

We aim to leverage CGD’s influence on donor institutions and other high-level decision-makers, positioning ourselves both as a go-to resource for learning and a level of accountability, guiding global leaders towards evidence-based policies and investments that improve development outcomes for people in LMICs. The Policy Fellow will define and undertake an agenda of policy analysis and outreach focused on issues of high importance to the global development community, with a focus on AI. The Policy Fellow should be expert in current issues surrounding AI, and should be familiar with the current international institutions and forums central to AI policy discussions.

This is a full-time position based in Washington, D.C or London.

The Policy Fellow’s principal responsibilities will include:

  • Collaboratively setting the intellectual vision and research and policy agenda for the team

  • Conducting research and policy analysis in areas of expertise, including but not limited to AI specific evaluation methods (evaluation of AI interventions and AI for evaluation), emerging technologies, and development effectiveness.

  • Ensuring that research and policy analysis are translated into concrete actions and impact by establishing collaborative relationships with policymakers, development agencies, donors, and international financial institutions

  • Engaging in related policy outreach activities, including speaking engagements, representing the organization at a prominent level in meetings, conferences, presentations, expert group consultations, working groups, technical communities, and other forums; and publishing blogs, papers, policy briefs, and/or short commentaries geared towards policymakers, academics, and CGD’s public audience

  • Organizing and facilitating private meetings and public events in areas of expertise

  • Mobilizing financial resources and support for the program and its staff in close coordination and cooperation with fundraising staff and CGD leadership

  • Supervising mid-level and junior staff and being accountable for their performance management and development

  • Overseeing planning, budgeting, execution, methods, and staff to achieve the program’s goals

  • Engaging with and contributing to the institution’s wider initiatives around diversity, equity and inclusion, as well as playing a key part in creating a culture which aligns with our mission and values

  • Integrating activities within the program and across the organization

  • Developing and supporting solutions to complex problems requiring a high degree of ingenuity, creativity, engagement, and innovation

The successful candidate possesses the following qualifications:

  • PhD or Master’s in economics, international development, public policy, technology policy, computer science, or a closely related discipline, with substantive work on development issues.

  • 12 or more years of policy experience.

  • Publication and impact record – Demonstrated ability to produce rigorous research (peer-reviewed articles, working papers, or flagship policy reports) that has influenced or aimed to influence development policy debates.

  • Exceptional communication skills – Proven aptitude for distilling complex analytics into concise, persuasive writing and presentations for both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Field & stakeholder experience – Prior collaboration with LMIC governments, multilaterals, or NGOs; familiarity with research ethics, data-protection regulations, and the practicalities of implementing evaluations in resource-constrained settings.

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, as well as high level organizational skills

  • Ability to work collaboratively within the multidisciplinary team while remaining individually accountable for delivering on policy outreach

  • Demonstrated leadership and management skills. Ability to coach junior staff such as research assistants.

Interested candidates should submit a Resume.

CGD offers a work environment that is collegial, rewarding, and rich with opportunities for intellectual and professional growth. The compensation package includes generous paid time off, a robust medical, vision and dental benefits with a modest employee contribution, employer retirement contribution, commuter benefits, and much more. The organization is working hybrid with all staff required to be in the office at least three days per week. CGD is registered to employ staff living in DC, Maryland, or Virginia. Candidates must be able to live and work in one of these locations to be considered.

item.title: Post Doctoral Research Associate in Agent-Based Climate Macroeconomics at University of Oxford (UK)
item.description: The University of Oxford is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate to contribute to research examining the macroeconomic impacts of UK climate mitigation policies.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The University of Oxford is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate to contribute to research examining the macroeconomic impacts of UK climate mitigation policies. Based at the Institute for New Economic Thinking (INET), the successful candidate will join the MacroCB7 – Macroeconomics of the Seventh Carbon Budget project, working closely with the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) to assess how climate policies affect economic growth, employment, inflation and inequality.

Working with Professor Doyne Farmer, Tom Youngman and Dr Donal Brown, you will contribute to the development and application of an innovative agent-based macroeconomic model to evaluate the economic and distributional consequences of net zero policies. Research will explore areas including low-carbon heating technologies, government finances, alternative investment scenarios and the potential for social tipping points in climate transitions.

The role combines quantitative research, software development and policy engagement. You will develop and implement new modelling approaches using Python, analyse results through sensitivity testing and simulation, contribute to academic publications, and present findings to government and policy partners. From June 2027, the research will expand to examine transformative net zero policies across energy, housing, transport and food, with a particular focus on reducing inequality alongside greenhouse gas emissions.

We are seeking candidates who hold, or are close to completion of, a PhD/DPhil in a relevant discipline, with programming experience and a strong understanding of economic theory, particularly macroeconomics and complexity approaches. You should have excellent analytical and communication skills, experience contributing to research publications, and an interest in applying quantitative modelling to climate policy. Experience in agent-based modelling, collaborative coding or policy-engaged research would be advantageous.

The role is based at INET’s offices on Manor Road, Oxford. Flexible working arrangements may be considered, subject to discussion and approval, including part-time working at 0.5 FTE or above. A minimum of one day per week in the office during term time is expected.

This position offers the opportunity to develop and apply innovative economic modelling methods to inform UK climate policy, working within an interdisciplinary research team with established government partnerships.

item.title: Economist in Distributional Impact of Policies Unit at World Bank
item.description: At the World Bank, a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
At the World Bank, a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. For more information, visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/who-we-are/ibrd

Within this architecture, the Prosperity vertical helps countries accelerate inclusive growth and job creation; strengthen macro-fiscal foundations, including debt sustainability, debt management, domestic resource mobilization, and expenditure efficiency; promote a resilient and inclusive financial sector, business‑enabling policies and regulations, and trade facilitation; while advancing transparent, effective, accountable institutions. The Distributional Impact of Policies Global unit in the Fiscal Policy and Growth Department focuses on integrating distributional analysis of reforms and investments into operational knowledge and lending and comprises applied microeconomists, statisticians, data scientists, and social and behavioral scientists who support WBG teams and governments to ensure that WBG interventions and country policies and programs reduce poverty and inequality in a sustainable manner.

Duties and Accountabilities:

The Distributional Impact of Policies unit is looking for an Economist to join our team, based in Washington, DC. The successful candidate will have the following duties:

• Design and implement cutting edge analytics on poverty and equity that provide policy relevant guidance and foster public debate, including acting as a team member on global reports.
• Support the development of micro-empirical models to examine the linkages between welfare, fiscal and social policies, incorporating spatial dimensions as appropriate.
• Develop and apply innovative analytical frameworks, tools, and technologies to assess spatial disparities and the distributional impact of policies.
• Support country teams in integrating geospatial and subnational fiscal analytics that can strengthen operational engagement and inform policy dialogue.
• Provide support to country teams in the design of operations, and in strengthening data systems to underpin evidence-based policymaking.
• Contribute to the production of public goods and knowledge products and facilitate knowledge flows between country and global teams.
• Contribute to corporate engagement of the Department, including reviews, preparation of briefs and policy notes on thematic issues, and the delivery of just-in-time rapid analytics and diagnostics.

Selection Criteria

A Master’s degree (PhD preferred) in economics, public policy, or other related field with a strong quantitative background, solid programming skills, and at least five years of relevant professional experience.

Technical competencies:

• Strong analytical and quantitative skills, with demonstrated experience in performing complex econometric analysis and statistical modeling, and the ability to translate findings into actionable recommendations for strategies, policies, and programs for poverty and inequality reduction.
• Demonstrated experience integrating geospatial and household survey data to analyze the spatial dimensions of poverty and inequality, including geographic disparities in public service delivery, infrastructure, and the effects of subnational fiscal policies using GIS, remote sensing, and econometric methods.
• Demonstrated in-depth expertise in at least two (2) of the following technical areas: poverty mapping/small area estimation techniques, spatial econometrics and modelling; processing and management of big data sources; and fiscal analysis with a subnational focus, including experience using revenue and expenditure data and the analysis of distributional impacts of tax and expenditure policies.
• Experience in the design and delivery of technical training and workshops, effectively communicating complex methodological content to diverse audiences including government counterparts, researchers, and practitioners across varying levels of technical expertise and adapting training content and delivery to different regional and institutional contexts.
• Excellent communication skills, including the ability to present technical findings and policy implications clearly and compellingly to a wide range of audiences (such as senior management, policymakers, academic audiences, and the public); and to produce high-quality written outputs (such as technical papers, policy notes, and presentations) that are well-structured and accessible.

Given the fast-paced, global nature of the unit’s engagement, the candidate must demonstrate strong teamwork and organizational skills:

• Solid organizational and project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple deliverables simultaneously and meet tight deadlines.
• Flexibility and adaptability in a dynamic work environment where priorities may shift rapidly.
• Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and take initiative with minimal supervision while remaining aligned with team objectives and institutional priorities.
• Ability to work flexibly, creatively, and to multitask as the need arises. High degree of self-motivation, positive attitude, commitment, and drive.
• Superb interpersonal skills, ability to collaborate effectively with multi-disciplinary teams, and to listen to and integrate ideas from diverse sources, governments, NGOs and donors, while being respectful and sensitive to cultural, political and gender issues.
• Ability to work with staff from all levels.

As the World Bank Group continues to evolve, we value candidates who:

  • Demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively across teams, disciplines, cultures, and institutional boundaries.

  • Responsibly leverage digital and AI-enabled tools to enhance productivity, learning, and decision-making.

  • Bring experience working in fragile, conflict-affected, and violent (FCV) contexts and are encouraged to highlight relevant experience in their application materials, where applicable.

WBG Culture Attributes:

1. Sense of urgency: Anticipate and quickly respond to the needs of internal and external stakeholders.
2. Thoughtful risk-taking: Challenge the status quo and push boundaries to achieve greater impact.
3. Empowerment and accountability: Empower yourself and others to act and hold each other accountable for results.

World Bank Group Core Competencies

The World Bank Group offers comprehensive benefits, including a retirement plan; medical, life and disability insurance; and paid leave, including parental leave, as well as reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity and inclusive employer with a dedicated and committed workforce, and do not discriminate based on gender, gender identity, religion, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or disability.
